name: Meridian
summary: A payments and ledger workspace that helps engineers move from API evaluation to a confident first integration.
scope: Developer journey · Information architecture · API explorer · Documentation
alt: Meridian payments API workspace with a guided quickstart and runnable request panel.
intro: Turn a complex payments API into a sequence developers can understand, test, and take to production.
overview: Meridian is a payments and ledger developer workspace I designed around the moments that determine adoption: evaluating a capability, configuring safe access, making the first call, recovering from errors, tracing events, and preparing for production.
decisions: Keep guidance beside execution
The API reference and runnable request share one working context so developers can learn a field, change a value, and inspect the response without rebuilding context across tools.
Make recovery part of the flow
Authentication, permission, and validation failures each explain the cause and the next corrective action, so a developer can retry without starting over.
Separate request and delivery state
A successful payment or ledger write is distinct from webhook delivery. Stable IDs and attempt history make the operational relationship visible.
Make production readiness explicit
A launch checklist carries the journey beyond a green sandbox response into credentials, idempotency, observability, versioning, and data controls.
gallery: Sandbox application setup with task-specific access and a visible environment boundary.
API reference and implementation guidance organized around the developer’s next decision.
Runnable request playground with code, inputs, and a response contract in one view.
Actionable error recovery that names the cause, corrective change, and retry path.
Webhook attempts remain traceable to the originating request without collapsing delivery state.
Production-readiness review turns operational responsibilities into explicit decisions.

name: API Launchpad
summary: An API developer workspace that connects discovery, first call, debugging, and operational readiness.
scope: Journey strategy · Information architecture · Interaction design · Prototype
alt: API Launchpad developer workspace showing a guided three-step API integration path.
intro: Help developers move from API evaluation to a confident first integration.
overview: API Launchpad is a developer platform experience I designed to keep documentation, execution, error recovery, event delivery, and readiness in one coherent workspace.
decisions: Keep guidance beside execution
The API reference and runnable request share a workspace so developers can understand a field, change a value, and inspect the response without rebuilding context across separate tools.
Turn errors into recovery paths

Authentication, permission, and validation failures each identify a distinct cause and the next corrective action. The prototype lets an interviewer trigger a failure, apply the suggested fix, and retry in place.
Separate business state from delivery state

A successful reconciliation and an acknowledged webhook are treated as different milestones. Stable event IDs and an attempt history make retry behavior visible without implying that a successful API response guarantees downstream delivery.
Make production readiness explicit
The final checklist carries the journey beyond a green sandbox response into credential lifecycle, idempotency, observability, versioning, and financial-data controls.

name: Enta
summary: Connecting everyday payments and digital assets in one account.
alt: Enta public product demo showing account balances, recent transactions and receive controls
intro: One account. Clearer choices for moving and holding money.
overview: Enta combines cross-border money movement with digital asset balances in a shared workspace.
challenge: Make currencies, destinations, fees and transaction states understandable without requiring people to become experts in payment infrastructure.
decisions: Start with the destination

The send experience distinguishes an Enta wallet, an external address, and a bank account before asking for route-specific details. This choice helps people recognize what they are trying to do while giving the interface a clear basis for the information it asks for next.
Explain both sides of a purchase

The purchase interface separates what the customer pays from what they receive. Asset selection, conversion and review belong to one continuous decision, so the customer can assess the exchange before following payment instructions.
Keep the balance connected to the next action

The wallet view combines an aggregate balance with individual holdings and a move-money action. The hierarchy supports a quick overview while retaining the currency and network context needed to act deliberately.

name: Metric OS
summary: Making system performance easier to understand.
alt: Metric OS incident workspace with service topology, correlated logs and a rollback recommendation
intro: From a storm of alerts to a clear next action.
overview: Metric OS connects telemetry, service dependencies, and incident investigation in one workspace. It helps engineering teams understand what changed, who is affected, and which response is safe.
challenge: Teams had plenty of monitoring data but little shared context. Switching between logs, traces, infrastructure metrics, and conversations made it difficult to connect symptoms to causes.
decisions: Group signals into an incident
Correlated alerts become a single investigation with the affected services, suspected origin, and confidence visible.
Keep topology and evidence connected
A split workspace shows service relationships alongside the supporting logs. Investigation stays within one operational context.
Make remediation accountable
A rollback recommendation includes supporting evidence, expected impact, permission requirements, and post-action verification.
outcome: The design provides a continuous path from detection to investigation and governed remediation. Evaluation focuses on time to assigned action, time spent reconciling evidence, and confidence in the response workflow.
gallery: System-health overview: service availability, signal composition, latency, capacity, and resolution work share a common context. Interface values are sample data.
Investigation detail: correlated logs and a root-cause hypothesis lead into an explicit action review. Sample incident data illustrates the interaction.

name: Sendory
summary: Turning reusable components into polished newsletters.
scope: Innovation concept, composition workflow and interactive prototype
alt: Sendory newsletter builder with a component palette, live canvas and contextual properties
intro: Make a polished newsletter without starting from a blank page.
overview: Sendory brings templates, reusable layout structures and content blocks into a visual newsletter workspace.
challenge: Help authors compose with confidence while retaining the flexibility to shape each edition.
decisions: Offer a useful starting point

Three starter templates—Client digest, Announcement and Editorial brief—give an author a structure to adapt. The choice is based on the communication they want to create, so they can begin with a recognizable purpose and refine the content without first arranging every section.
Separate structure from content

The palette distinguishes eight layout structures from 24 content blocks. Columns and containers define the space; headlines, cards, images, events and calls to action fill it. That separation lets a reusable layout support different stories rather than locking every newsletter into one finished design.
Make controls follow the selection

Selecting a content block exposes its content and typography controls. Selecting a layout exposes spacing, direction and background controls. Keeping these property groups contextual lets the author focus on the decision at hand while seeing the composition beside it.
gallery: Three existing starter templates offer a purpose-led beginning: Client digest, Announcement and Editorial brief.
Searching the palette narrows the reusable content blocks; the selected card exposes its own editing controls. Demonstration content.
Layout selection exposes direction, spacing, padding and background controls rather than text formatting.

name: Flownode
summary: Making AI automation understandable and controllable—from a plain-language idea to a workflow people can inspect.
scope: Workflow experience · Interface design · Interactive prototype
alt: Flownode prototype showing a connected workflow with branching steps and a human approval gate.
intro: Turning an automation idea into a visible, editable plan—without losing human control.
overview: An AI workflow authoring and operations concept.
challenge: Make generated automation understandable before execution.
decisions: Review a plan before inserting it

The AI builder presents a proposed sequence, the purpose of each step, and an estimated credit cost before the workflow reaches the canvas. This creates a deliberate review moment: a person can check whether the proposed automation matches their intent. In the prototype, plan generation uses predefined examples; the interaction demonstrates how a future model-backed experience could make its proposal inspectable.
Keep the workflow visible while editing a step

The canvas establishes the overall sequence while a configuration panel supports detailed changes. This arrangement gives people a way to understand where a decision sits in the larger process. A human approval gate is represented as an explicit node, making a sensitive handoff part of the workflow rather than an invisible exception.
Give operations its own workspace

Execution history and the operations view separate authoring from day-to-day oversight. Status labels help distinguish successful, waiting, running, and failed work, while routing and failure views suggest where investigation should begin. The displayed metrics are demonstration data, used to explore hierarchy and decision support rather than report product performance.
gallery: Product overview in the interactive prototype. Credit, performance, and activity values are demo data.

Step configuration alongside the workflow canvas.

name: Agent OS
summary: Making an AI agent platform easier to understand, explore, and evaluate.
scope: Information architecture · Product storytelling · Web experience
alt: Agent OS homepage with a bold introduction and computing imagery.
intro: From an abstract AI promise to a clear path through capabilities, workflows, and plans.
overview: A connected product-discovery website for an AI agent platform.
challenge: Help visitors connect a broad AI proposition to a relevant capability and a clear next step.
decisions: Separate the promise from the explanation

The homepage establishes the broad proposition, while Agents, Platform, and Workflows provide distinct routes into the detail. This creates several starting points for visitors with different questions. The tradeoff is that those destinations must explain their relationship clearly enough to avoid making the visitor assemble the product story alone.
Make workflows a bridge to relevance

A list of capabilities can describe what a platform contains without explaining what someone could do with it. Giving workflows their own destination creates space to connect agents with a sequence of work. The intended benefit is comprehension: visitors should be able to describe an applicable scenario before evaluating a plan.
Put plan differences side by side

The pricing page uses Starter, Pro, and Enterprise cards to organize scope and support differences. Repeated feature structures make comparison easier, while distinct calls to action suggest a next step. In the prototype, those links lead to contact; the experience demonstrates an evaluation path rather than an operational subscription checkout.

Workflow explanation as a bridge from capabilities to use.

name: IreTV
summary: Meaningful stories. A clearer path to play.
scope: Product strategy, UX architecture, interface design
alt: IreTV welcome experience with cinematic imagery and clear paths into faith-centered entertainment
intro: From discovering a meaningful story to pressing play with confidence.
overview: IreTV is my independent streaming-platform project. It brings Christian films, series, live television, children’s programming, podcasts, radio, and devotionals into one product. The central design challenge is to give that breadth a clear structure while helping a viewer make a confident choice about what to watch.
challenge: A faith-centered catalog needs to communicate more than availability. Viewers need enough story and content context to choose confidently, a clear distinction between saving and accessing a title, and a dependable path back to their viewing. If those states blur together, a visually rich interface can still leave basic questions unanswered.
decisions: Organize around viewing intent

The product architecture connects discovery, evaluation, access, playback, and return. Curated collections provide an editorial entry point while the library supports a different task: finding something already saved or started.
Make access understandable before commitment

The current first-film page presents the price, viewing window, and absence of a subscription beside the primary action. Earlier prototype rental terms differed; the launch-specific offer replaces those assumptions rather than inheriting them silently.
Build continuity beyond the first play

Watchlists, history, and saved progress support the return journey. The interface separates interest from entitlement and gives unfinished viewing its own place. This makes the library part of the core experience rather than an account-management afterthought.
outcome: The work connects product strategy, a detailed UX specification, reusable interface patterns, and an implemented streaming experience. The saved iterations demonstrate how discovery, title context, and return viewing were structured; the current screens show the IreTV identity and first-film offer. The documented controlled rental and playback are a concrete milestone, with their limits kept visible.
gallery: Earlier catalog iteration from the project archive, using inherited Mighty Arrow branding and sample titles. Featured content, curated rows, and return viewing establish the discovery hierarchy.
Earlier title-detail prototype: story context and a Faith & Family Guide support evaluation. Sample title data and rental pricing are design content, not the current live offer.
Earlier library prototype: active viewing, Watchlist, and History are separate tasks. Progress values are prototype data.

name: ArtoQu
summary: A clearer view of spending, savings, and everyday money.
scope: Dashboard experience · Financial information hierarchy · Interactive prototype
intro: Connecting everyday financial activity to the bigger picture.
overview: A web dashboard connecting savings goals, cash flow, wallet balances, and transaction detail.
challenge: Help people move from a financial summary to the detail needed to understand it.
decisions: Bring goals into the everyday overview

Savings targets appear alongside cash flow and account context, connecting longer-term intentions to the routine act of checking money. Each target combines a label, time horizon, amount, and progress indicator. This hierarchy is intended to make goals recognizable without requiring a separate planning session. The prototype’s sample values illustrate the layout; calculation consistency remains a validation priority.
Give transactions a dedicated workspace

The overview introduces recent activity, while the transaction screen provides space for deeper inspection. This separation keeps the first screen focused and gives people a predictable destination when they need to investigate an amount or category. The design question is whether the transition preserves enough context to explain the summary.
Separate account context from trend analysis

Wallet and statistics views support different questions: where money is held and how activity changes over time. Persistent navigation connects these views while allowing each to use a suitable information hierarchy. Balance cards emphasize account context; charts emphasize comparison. Neither should require people to infer the period or meaning of an amount.

Wallet view showing account and balance context in the prototype.

name: Pulse
summary: Making payment operations traceable from quote to settlement.
alt: Pulse public test-mode dashboard showing business performance and settlement by asset
intro: Clear operational control over complex money movement.
overview: Pulse connects collection, conversion and payout with a partner console for monitoring and investigation.
challenge: Help teams distinguish a customer payment from completed settlement and investigate exceptions with a shared transaction record.
decisions: Separate paid from settled

The transaction table keeps the pegged amount, customer payment and final settlement in separate columns. A completed deposit is meaningful progress, but it does not establish that the partner received the expected value. This distinction makes reconciliation more precise.
Bring the exception and its evidence together

The detail view starts with the underpayment warning and the difference between expected and received amounts. A timeline then connects that exception to the remaining conversion and settlement steps, so the operator can explain what happened without assembling a story from disconnected records.
Make integration health visible

Webhook endpoints expose delivery performance and status within the same console used for payment operations. This gives developers a place to assess the communication path while finance and operations retain transaction-level evidence.

Underpayment review connects expected and received amounts with a transaction timeline and settlement details. Public demo data.

name: Arca
summary: Balances, budgets, and card controls in one calm mobile experience.
scope: Mobile experience · Financial hierarchy · Interactive prototype
alt: Arca mobile wallet overview with sample balances and money actions.
intro: A calmer way to understand money and find the next action.
overview: A mobile wallet concept connecting financial orientation, activity, and card management.
challenge: Make a dense set of financial tasks understandable on a small screen.
decisions: Establish the overview before the actions

The home screen leads with a total balance and period controls, then places common money actions within reach. Card summaries, budgets, and recent activity provide supporting context further down the screen. This layered hierarchy aims to support a quick check while keeping detail available for a longer visit. The relationship between the total and individual sample balances needs reconciliation before evaluating numerical trust.
Give activity a stable destination

Activity has a dedicated place in the bottom navigation, allowing someone to move from a broad summary to a record of individual events. This separates checking a balance from investigating why it changed. Evaluation should establish whether transaction descriptions, amounts, and categories give enough context without requiring unnecessary navigation.
Keep card controls beside card context

The Cards destination places management actions near the selected card, with masked details and spending information below. This makes the object of an action visible before someone chooses it. Controls such as Freeze and Limits are prototype representations; the interface does not establish a connection to a card issuer or a real security service.

name: ShiftSnap
summary: Clearer schedules for people working in shifts.
alt: ShiftSnap mobile scheduling and shift management screens
intro: Helping hourly workers stay on top of their day.
overview: ShiftSnap brings shift management into a focused mobile experience, helping hourly workers understand schedules and coordinate changes.
challenge: Shift changes require clear status and dependable communication. Workers need to know what is scheduled, what is pending, and which action comes next.
decisions: Make schedules easy to find
The experience prioritizes upcoming work and the information needed to plan the day.
Clarify shift changes
Swap and request flows make the action and its status visible.
Keep the experience mobile-first
Focused screens support quick checks and everyday coordination.
outcome: The product design connects onboarding and shift management in a consistent mobile experience. The complete experience board below shows the core flows and screen relationships.

name: Interoly
summary: Stock and order context, close to the work.
scope: Information architecture · Operational workflows · Interactive prototype
alt: Interoly prototype overview with demonstration data.
intro: Stock and order context, close to the work.
overview: Interoly connects an overview to dedicated operational destinations.
challenge: Help people connect a summary to the record and status needed to understand it.
decisions: Surface work needing attention

The home screen calls out items below reorder level and groups sales activity by operational status. This creates a starting point for deciding where to look next. The design hypothesis is that a visible exception and a direct route to review are more useful during a short visit than a collection of equally emphasized metrics.
Keep item inspection in its own destination

Items has a stable position in the bottom navigation, giving stock inspection a predictable home. A mobile catalog must help someone recognize the correct item before any adjustment is considered. The observed prototype supports exploring the item destination; barcode matching and live stock synchronization are not established by this walkthrough.
Make order status easy to inspect

The Orders destination gives individual work a stable place outside the overview. Visible records and status labels support inspection before action. A production implementation would need precise definitions for each status, clear ownership, and reliable feedback after a change; the screenshots show demonstration data rather than verified fulfilment activity.

name: ShopPulse
summary: Connecting store performance to the products and orders behind it.
scope: Information architecture · Operational workflows · Interactive prototype
alt: ShopPulse prototype overview with demonstration data.
intro: Connecting store performance to the products and orders behind it.
overview: ShopPulse connects an overview to dedicated operational destinations.
challenge: Help people connect a summary to the record and status needed to understand it.
decisions: Start with a performance overview

The dashboard establishes a broad view before someone moves into a dedicated management workspace. This supports the transition from noticing a performance signal to investigating its cause. Metric labels, reporting periods, and the relationship between aggregate figures and records remain essential to whether that transition is understandable.
Connect summaries to product context

The Products destination separates catalog inspection from the overview. It gives individual records room to be read without crowding the dashboard. A consistent route to this detail should help an operator connect a broad signal to the product context that might explain it, a hypothesis to evaluate with realistic tasks.
Make order status easy to inspect

The Orders destination gives individual work a stable place outside the overview. Visible records and status labels support inspection before action. A production implementation would need precise definitions for each status, clear ownership, and reliable feedback after a change; the screenshots show demonstration data rather than verified fulfilment activity.

name: UrbanDrive
summary: From finding the right vehicle to understanding the rental.
scope: Search experience · Vehicle comparison · Booking flow
intro: A clearer path from travel plans to a considered rental choice.
overview: A car rental frontend connecting search, fleet discovery, and booking configuration.
challenge: Connect a vehicle choice to understandable rental details before commitment.
decisions: Start with the trip

Location and rental dates sit close to the homepage proposition, making the practical task visible alongside vehicle imagery. Rental-mode choices suggest different travel needs. The design question is whether visitors can establish their trip context without being distracted by promotional content.
Make vehicles comparable

Fleet cards repeat daily rate, seating, transmission, and fuel information. Repeated structure supports scanning across alternatives while category controls narrow the collection. A daily rate is only an entry point: the booking experience still needs to explain duration, extras, and the total.
Keep rental context beside configuration

The rental-details screen places location, dates, and protection choices alongside a booking summary. This layout is intended to make the effect of a choice easier to inspect before advancing. The prototype contains sample dates and prices; synchronizing the summary with entered values is a priority for further evaluation.
gallery: Fleet discovery and vehicle comparison in the hosted prototype.

name: Solshine
summary: A complete website template for solar services and renewable-energy businesses.
scope: Full template design · Page layouts · Service discovery · Enquiry experience
intro: Making solar services easier to explore—and a reusable website easier to adapt.
overview: A full Framer template for renewable-energy service businesses.
challenge: Connect a clear service proposition to detailed information and a visible enquiry path.
decisions: Make the service proposition visible first

The homepage combines a direct solar-energy headline, relevant imagery, and an exploration link. This establishes the category before presenting the broader service collection. The template needs to work with different businesses, so the hierarchy should remain understandable when images and copy are replaced.
Give services repeatable structure

The service collection creates a predictable route into installation, maintenance, and related offerings. Repeated layouts help visitors compare the kinds of support available while giving a template adopter a consistent place to introduce each service. The content must still distinguish those offerings rather than repeat a generic value proposition.
Keep enquiry within reach

Get in touch appears in the main navigation and alongside service content, connecting exploration to a clear next step. The contact page gives the enquiry its own destination. This is a designed conversion path; no conversion-rate improvement or enquiry volume is claimed.
